content.text: How They Handle Restricted Countries

When it comes to restricted countries, Gumroad and COREMERCH have different approaches. Gumroad relies on Stripe's global network, which is often restricted in countries with strict KYC regulations. In contrast, COREMERCH's NOWPayments integration allows for seamless on-chain crypto payment processing, bypassing traditional payment gateways and their associated restrictions. This makes COREMERCH an ideal solution for creators operating in countries with restricted payment processing.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Payment speed and fees are critical considerations for digital creators. Gumroad's 10% fee may seem reasonable, but it translates to significant revenue loss for creators, particularly those selling high-ticket digital products. In contrast, COREMERCH's 0.5% fee, combined with NOWPayments' instant payment verification, ensures faster payment processing and lower transaction costs. For instance, at 100 sales per month on a $97 product, the fee difference retains $921 for the creator, a substantial savings that can be reinvested in their business.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Ownership, automation, and delivery are essential aspects of a digital product store. COREMERCH's infrastructure sovereignty ensures creators maintain full ownership of their digital store, data, and automated delivery. With Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, creators can automate delivery, eliminating manual intervention and ensuring a seamless customer experience. In contrast, Gumroad's reliance on Stripe means creators are tied to a third-party platform, limiting their control and flexibility.
Automated delivery means the download link arrives before the buyer navigates away from the payment confirmation page.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

The order management layer gives you complete visibility into every transaction your store processes. In Stack 01, every order is logged to a Google Sheet with the buyer's email, product purchased, payment amount in crypto and USD equivalent, transaction hash for on-chain verification, and delivery status. In Stack 02, orders are stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with the same fields plus additional metadata. Both can be exported as CSV at any time. The transaction hash provides cryptographic proof of every payment that does not depend on any platform's records — you can verify any transaction independently on a public blockchain explorer.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

Scaling a sovereign digital store requires no infrastructure changes at any realistic volume level for most individual creators. Cloudflare Workers processes each webhook event independently — ten simultaneous orders are handled as ten separate processes with no queue congestion. Supabase handles hundreds of concurrent database operations on the free tier. Resend delivers 3,000 emails per month on the free tier — enough for significant daily sales volume. Cloudflare Pages serves the storefront to any number of concurrent visitors without capacity constraints. NOWPayments processes payment volume without per-transaction approval delays.
